final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor supplied no new admissible evidence and instead narrowed the theory to a more policy-bounded position. That clarification is useful, but it does not cure the core evidentiary gap. The distinction is decisive: a caveat can support compliant_with_caveats only when the caveated condition is already satisfied and merely needs to be stated clearly. Here, the unresolved predicate is whether the required explicit limitation disclosure is actually present in the launch certification packet. On the available record, it is not proven. The Actor also concedes there is no approved risk acceptance and no exclusion of the affected use case. Under the stated policy, rollout controls, rollback, and monitoring do not substitute for that missing requirement while exposure remains. So the present certification claim remains inadequately supported from admissible evidence alone.
remaining_concerns: No admissible evidence shows the certification or model-card packet actually contains the required explicit field-service dispatch limitation disclosure.
The affected field-service dispatch use case remains exposed.
The available risk acceptance draft is unsigned and incomplete, so it is not admissible support.
Policy says rollout controls and monitoring mitigate this weakness only if the affected use case is excluded or reviewed risk acceptance exists; neither predicate is satisfied on this record.
Aggregate readiness, no severity-one incidents, 6% rollout, rollback capability, and public guidance are supportive context only and do not satisfy the policy-specific disclosure condition.
